claims.source_span: There is also a notion of an injective module, which is dual to the notion of a projective module. Namely, we have the following theorem.
claims.claim: Existence of a dual notion of injective module (introduction to Theorem 8.1.5)
claims.reason: Purely transitional prose pointing to Theorem 8.1.5; no standalone proposition is being stated. The actual mathematical content is in the numbered theorem that follows, which is formalized in Theorem8_1_5.lean.

claims.source_span: Theorem 8.1.1(iv) and Theorem 8.1.5(iii) can be used to define a projective and an injective object in any abelian category. Namely, we make the following definition.
claims.claim: The module characterizations of projective (Hom_A(P,?) exact) and injective (Hom_A(?,I) exact) generalize to define projective and injective objects in any abelian category.
claims.reason: Definition8_1_8.lean directly formalizes projective and injective objects in abelian categories as CategoryTheory.Projective and CategoryTheory.Injective, precisely capturing the content of this prose remark. The blob is motivation for that definition.

claims.source_span: the functors $M \otimes_A ?$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M, ?)$ (where $M$ is a right, respectively left, $A$-module) on the category of left $A$-modules are, in general, not exact (they are only exact on one side)
claims.claim: Tensor product M⊗_A? is right exact but not left exact; Hom_A(M,?) is left exact but not right exact.
claims.reason: The blob itself cross-references 'Example 7.9.6', which is formalized in Chapter7/Example7_9_6.lean with instances for left exactness of Hom and right exactness of tensor. Covered by the Chapter 7 formalization.

claims.source_span: The job of the functors $\mathrm{Tor}_i^A(M, ?)$ and $\mathrm{Ext}^i_A(M, ?)$ is to quantify the extent to which the functors $M \otimes_A ?$ and $\mathrm{Hom}_A(M, ?)$ fail to be exact. Namely, these functors are defined as follows.
claims.claim: Motivational description of Tor and Ext as derived functors quantifying failure of exactness (points to Definitions 8.2.3 and 8.2.4).
claims.reason: Purely motivational prose; the actual definitions are in Definition8.2.3.md and Definition8.2.4.md, already formalized in Definition8_2_3.lean and Definition8_2_4.lean.

claims.source_span: In a similar way one can define Tor and Ext groups in any abelian category which has **enough projectives**; i.e., any object is a quotient of a projective object (this condition insures that every object has a projective resolution).
claims.claim: An abelian category has enough projectives (every object is a quotient of a projective) if and only if every object has a projective resolution; under this condition, Tor and Ext can be defined.
claims.reason: The condition 'enough projectives' is CategoryTheory.EnoughProjectives in Mathlib, and Mathlib provides the instance EnoughProjectives → HasProjectiveResolutions. The Chapter8 Lean files already use HasProjectiveResolutions directly (Definition8_2_3.lean). The prose is a definitional remark and the content is fully captured by Mathlib infrastructure; there is no novel gap to formalize in this project.
